blocks.content:
Originally, the Supreme Court consisted of:
• One Chief Justice of India
• Seven other judges

Presently, Parliament has increased the strength.
Current sanctioned strength:
• Chief Justice of India + 33 judges = 34 judges total.

Parliament has the authority to increase the number of judges.
Parliament has the authority to increase the number of judges.

items: Parliament (and not the President) has the authority to increase the strength of Supreme Court judges.
The initial total strength of Supreme Court judges was 8, whereas the present sanctioned total strength is 34.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Originally, the Supreme Court comprised 1 Chief Justice of India and 7 other judges.
The present sanctioned strength stands at 34 judges (1 Chief Justice of India + 33 judges).
Parliament holds the statutory authority to increase the number of Supreme Court judges.
